review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). For d>=1, the note proves an intrinsic lower frontier and observable upper envelopes, but the optimized Gram upper scale is polynomially slower than the lower quadratic scale, so it does not determine the minimax rate in the central regime. The Gaussian–quadratic transition is proved only for an infeasible population-score, population-kernel statistic, while observable mixed-regime calibration remains open. Moreover, the asserted uniform equivalence sd(L) asymp rho_n/sqrt(n) is false for increasingly high outcome-frequency discrepancies: rho_n controls one antiderivative of the density discrepancy, whereas the Kantorovich score contains an additional smoothing, allowing V_{L,n}=o(rho_n^2). The matched d=0 result and exact Brownian-bridge law do not close the conditional d>=1 headline. The framing does not claim a matched bracket, but its recurring use of “frontier” can refer only to the proved lower benchmark, not to a settled conditional minimax frontier.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Replace the pilot-limited Gram construction with a higher-order or localized estimator whose pilot-discrepancy projection remainder is uniformly of order n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)} or smaller. Also replace the claimed uniform equivalence sd(L) asymp rho_n/sqrt(n) by a valid bound in terms of V_{L,n}, unless an additional low-outcome-frequency condition is proved.

The mixed spectral transition is proved only for an infeasible population-score, population-kernel statistic; neither observable quantile consistency nor an honest mixed-regime confidence procedure is delivered. review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). For d≥1, the central minimax theorem proves an intrinsic lower frontier but only a strictly slower observable upper envelope, so it does not determine the quadratic-zone rate. The growing-rank transition applies only to an infeasible population-score, population-kernel statistic, while the load-bearing observable mixed-regime calibration remains open. The isotropic transfer is likewise an unmatched bracket on a class constructed in the note rather than a resolution of the published SmoothCOT class. The TL;DR inaccurately attributes the entire lower frontier to the sign-paired family: its rho/sqrt(n) component actually requires the separate fixed-frequency two-point construction. The public [direct-COT](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.00257v2) and [SmoothCOT](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.20681v1) theorem texts support the cited global rates and regular CLT only, not equality-local optimality or observable mixed calibration.

Directed re-attempts exhausted: the named bounded improvements were tried and did not lift the tier. Lifting now needs new math (directed solve) or a re-anchored proposal — halting for the operator.
